who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code, dst-1113
where: blaze-vm, ending a check daemon left behind by a command /root/loop.sh stopped at 600 s
what: Two things in one. (1) A `blaze check` that loop.sh stops at its 600 s limit leaves its daemon running (`/root/inst/<branch>/blaze-engine serve`, here 657 s old at 29% CPU), because the `"$BLAZE" stop` after it in the same command never runs. (2) Ending it with `kill -9 $(pgrep -f "/root/inst/<branch>/blaze-engine serve")` inside `ix shell .. bash -c '..'` killed the shell that ran it: the pattern is in that shell's own command line, so the rest of the command (a `cat` of the smoke quote) printed nothing and I verified an empty quote before seeing why.
cost: one wrong `no blaze-smoke 1 line` verdict and a rerun; a daemon that ran ten minutes on a loaded machine
cause: loop.sh's timeout kills the command, not what the command started; `pgrep -f` matches its caller
whys: a daemon is started as a side effect of a client command and outlives it by design; the queue script bounds the command only; ending a daemon is by a pattern over command lines, which the ending command itself contains
class: a process a bounded command started that the bound does not end
prevention: loop.sh ends the branch's daemon itself when its command returns or is stopped (it already ends the old one before installing: the same three lines, after the command); until then, match with a bracketed first letter (`[b]laze-engine`) or by `BLAZE_HOME`'s pid file. Not built.
